entries.title: CLI update: package

ai.title: Prevent CLI crashes on WSL and headless Linux browser open
ai.summary: The `safeOpen` utility now explicitly checks for `powershell.exe` accessibility on WSL and attaches an error listener to the spawned process. This prevents uncaught exceptions that terminate the CLI when Windows interop is disabled or when `xdg-open` fails on headless Linux systems. The change adds `wsl-utils` as a dependency in `cli/package.json` to align path resolution with the underlying `open` library.

eli5.text: When you ask the program to open a webpage on a Windows-connected Linux setup or on a computer without a visible desktop, the program used to crash and stop working entirely. It now checks first whether the helper it needs is actually available, and if it isn't, it quietly skips the open attempt instead of failing. This keeps the program running so you can keep using it instead of being kicked out.

facts: "Premium"/"Unlimited" chip. The shared 0/5 counter lives in the page title (rendered by the parent), not the section header, this picker is purely a list of choices grouped by tier. Empty sections are filtered so a model set with no premium (or no unlimited) entries doesn't render an orphan header.
"BR" → "Brazil". Falls back to the raw code when the runtime can't resolve it (malformed code, missing ICU data).
Hidden in compact terminals: the notice is nice-to-have context, and below 22 rows every line competes with the picker itself.
Streak is rendered inline as a one-line row directly under the counter (landing) or title (queued), with the same bottom margin as its neighbor so the picker still sits flush below it.

Status lines render below the picker, each with marginTop 1: the session counter (landing only), then the limited-mode notice, then the streak. They still eat into the picker's height budget regardless of being above or below it.

ai.summary: CLI model selector layout updates. Premium/Unlimited headers now show reset countdowns and no-limit labels. Streak and limited-mode notices render below the picker. Compact terminals hide the notice. Country codes format to names with fallbacks.

eli5.text: When you open the list of assistant models in the command-line tool, the headers for Premium and Unlimited tiers now show how many free sessions you have left and when they reset, instead of just a plain label. The notice telling you that some models aren't available in your country, along with your usage streak, now appears below the model list rather than above it. If your terminal window is short (under 22 rows), that notice is hidden to keep the model picker readable. Country names like 'BR' are shown as 'Brazil' when possible, falling back to the code if the name can't be looked up.

ai.title: Web referral tiers: 4-month GitHub age gate
ai.summary: New `common/src/constants/freebuff-referral-tiers.ts` defines Web referral ladder (1/3/7 qualified referrals) scaling daily model limits and unlocking deploy watermark removal. Referrals require referred user's GitHub account to be at least 4 months old at signup (anti-farming), computed on calendar months. `FREEBUFF_WEB_REFERRAL_LIMIT` set to 20 to bound farming while accommodating unqualified signups, distinct from CLI's `user.referral_limit` default of 5.

eli5.text: When you sign up for Freebuff through a friend's referral link on the web, your friend now earns a higher reward only if your GitHub account is at least 4 months old at the time you join. Younger accounts can still sign up, but the referring friend won't get credit for them. Each additional qualified referral raises the referrer's tier in a four-step ladder (1, 3, or 7 qualified referrals), increasing their daily usage limits and eventually removing the 'Powered by Freebuff' watermark from their deployed projects. A new cap of 20 attributed web signups per referrer keeps this from being abused, and the first tier unlocking watermark removal requires just one qualified referral.
